Craft / September 8, 2026 / 3 min read

Movement, with meaning.

A considered approach to motion, material, and the spaces between.

Motion creates relationships.

A transition can explain where something came from and where it is going. A gentle change in scale can signal focus. These are useful jobs for animation. Movement becomes distracting when it asks for attention without offering information in return.

Work with the reading pace.

A page is not a film. The visitor controls the pace and may move forward, back, or pause. Scroll-driven experiences should honor that control. Keep navigation available, avoid trapping the visitor, and make the essential content readable before any sequence completes.

Material changes the feeling.

A reflective surface moves differently from paper. Thinking about weight, light, and physical reference makes small interactions more coherent. The goal is not to imitate reality perfectly, but to create a consistent sense of touch.

Design the still version first.

Reduced motion is a first-class version of the experience. Content, hierarchy, and controls must work without choreography. When a page is compelling at rest, animation can add depth without becoming a dependency.
